title: Medical AI has a measurement problem
excerpt: The development of two medical AI assistants highlights an unnerving challenge: as the technology races ahead, what is the best way to evaluate what works?
content_html:
• NEWS AND VIEWS
  • 28 July 2026

The development of two medical AI assistants highlights an unnerving challenge: as the technology races ahead, what is the best way to evaluate what works?

By

  • Arjun K. Manrai0
  1. Arjun K. Manrai

    1. Arjun K. Manrai is in the Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School, Boston, Massachusetts 02115, USA.

Evidence-based medicine rests on the assumption that the yardstick used to measure the effectiveness of a new drug or medical device is reliable. But this assumption is often shaky, especially in the context of the artificial-intelligence tools that are making their way into clinical practice. Two papers in Nature, one by Ferber et al.1 and one by Liévin et al.2 show how capable medical AI tools have become, but also demonstrate why that capability is increasingly difficult to assess and understand properly.

• 新闻和观点
  • 28 July 2026

两名医疗人工智能助手的开发凸显了一个令人不安的挑战：随着技术的飞速发展，评估有效方法的最佳方法是什么？

By

  • 阿琼·K. 曼莱0
  1. 阿琼·K. 曼莱·阿琼·K. Manrai 就职于哈佛医学院生物医学信息学系，波士顿，马萨诸塞州 02115，美国。

循证医学基于这样的假设：用于衡量新药或医疗器械有效性的标准是可靠的。 但这种假设往往是站不住脚的，尤其是在人工智能工具正在进入临床实践的背景下。 《自然》杂志上的两篇论文，一篇由 Ferber 等人发表，另一篇由 Liévin 等人发表，2 展示了医疗人工智能工具的能力如何，但也证明了为什么这种能力越来越难以正确评估和理解。
